params.question: In the infertility workup, which investigation specifically evaluates the uterine cavity for polyps and submucous fibroids?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: HSG evaluates tubal patency by looking for contrast spill into the peritoneal cavity, not uterine cavity morphology.
Correct. Saline infusion sonohysterography distends the uterine cavity with fluid, allowing polyps and submucous fibroids to appear as filling defects against the fluid background.
The antral follicle count assesses ovarian reserve — the number of small follicles in the ovaries — not the uterine cavity.
HyCoSy is the radiation-free alternative to HSG for assessing tubal patency, not cavity abnormalities.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the modality-matching principle: saline infusion sonohysterography distends the endometrial cavity with saline during ultrasound, making it the specific test for cavity lesions like polyps and submucous fibroids.
Well done. Each infertility question has a specific imaging modality: TVS for ovarian reserve, HSG or HyCoSy for tubal patency, and saline infusion sonohysterography for the uterine cavity.

interactions.label: Which of the following is the most specific direct ultrasound sign of tubal ecto

params.question: Which of the following is the most specific direct ultrasound sign of tubal ectopic pregnancy?

answers.text: An empty uterus when serum β-hCG exceeds the discriminatory zone

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An empty uterus above the discriminatory zone is strongly suggestive but is an indirect sign — it shows what is absent (an intrauterine pregnancy), not what is present at the ectopic site.

answers.text: Echogenic free fluid in the Pouch of Douglas

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Echogenic fluid suggests blood and warns of tubal leakage or rupture, but it is not specific to ectopic pregnancy and can occur in other conditions.

answers.text: A tubal ring in the adnexa, separate from the ovary

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The tubal ring — an echogenic ring lying separate from the ovary — is the most specific direct sign of tubal ectopic pregnancy. A yolk sac or cardiac activity within it confirms the diagnosis.

answers.text: A centrally placed fluid collection within the endometrial cavity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes a pseudosac — a trap, not a sign of ectopic. It has no yolk sac and no double decidual sign. It can mimic a true gestational sac and must never falsely reassure you.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the three findings pointing to tubal ectopic: empty uterus above the discriminatory zone (indirect), tubal ring separate from the ovary (most specific direct sign), and echogenic free fluid. The pseudosac is a trap, not a diagnostic sign.
Correct. The tubal ring is the most specific direct sign because it shows the ectopic implantation site itself, unlike indirect signs such as an empty uterus or free fluid.

interactions.label: A 24-year-old woman has regular menstrual cycles and no clinical or biochemical

params.question: A 24-year-old woman has regular menstrual cycles and no clinical or biochemical evidence of hyperandrogenism. Her transvaginal ultrasound shows 22 follicles of 2–9 mm in one ovary. What is the correct interpretation?

answers.text: She has polycystic ovary syndrome based on the ultrasound finding

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Rotterdam requires any two of three criteria. With regular cycles and no hyperandrogenism, only one criterion (polycystic morphology) is met — that is insufficient for diagnosis.

answers.text: The ultrasound is diagnostic of PCOS since the follicle count exceeds the modern threshold

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While ≥20 follicles on modern TVS satisfies the morphology criterion, ultrasound provides only one of three Rotterdam criteria. It can never make the diagnosis alone.

answers.text: The finding is entirely normal in a young woman and needs no follow-up

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ≥22 follicles exceeds the polycystic morphology threshold (≥20 on modern TVS). Although it does not diagnose PCOS without a second criterion, polycystic morphology as an incidental finding warrants monitoring for metabolic risk.

answers.text: She meets one Rotterdam criterion; at least one more is needed before diagnosing PCOS

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Polycystic ovarian morphology is one of three Rotterdam criteria. With regular cycles (no oligo-anovulation) and no hyperandrogenism, only one criterion is met. Diagnosis requires any two of three, after excluding mimics such as thyroid disease and congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall that Rotterdam requires ANY two of three criteria. Ultrasound morphology alone — no matter how many follicles — is only one criterion. Without oligo-anovulation or hyperandrogenism, PCOS cannot be diagnosed, though the morphology warrants metabolic monitoring.
Well done. The scan is supportive, never sufficient. Rotterdam requires any two of three: oligo-anovulation, hyperandrogenism, and polycystic morphology — and mimics must be excluded first.

interactions.label: An infertility workup reveals bilateral tubal block with a hydrosalpinx on the l

params.question: An infertility workup reveals bilateral tubal block with a hydrosalpinx on the left side. The couple is counselled for in vitro fertilisation. What must be done before starting the IVF cycle?

answers.text: Begin controlled ovarian stimulation for IVF immediately

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Hydrosalpinx fluid is toxic to implantation. Starting IVF without treating the hydrosalpinx significantly reduces the chance of successful embryo implantation.

answers.text: Treat the hydrosalpinx before proceeding with the IVF cycle

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The narration states explicitly that a hydrosalpinx must be treated before IVF because its fluid is toxic to implantation. Even though bilateral block already directs the couple to IVF, this step is mandatory.

answers.text: Assess the uterine cavity with saline infusion sonohysterography first

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While cavity assessment is part of a thorough infertility workup, the immediate priority when a hydrosalpinx is identified is treating it before IVF, since its fluid impairs implantation.

answers.text: Repeat hysterosalpingography after three months to confirm the block

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Hydrosalpinx does not resolve spontaneously, and delaying treatment wastes valuable time. Bilateral block already directs management toward IVF; the hydrosalpinx requires intervention, not re-confirmation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: a hydrosalpinx contains fluid that is toxic to implantation. Even when bilateral tubal block already indicates IVF, the hydrosalpinx must be treated first. No single result drives infertility management — weigh all five factors together.
Correct. A hydrosalpinx is not merely a blocked tube — its fluid is embryotoxic. Treating it before IVF is a mandatory step to protect implantation.
